newsitem.title: UK: Soldiers fired on, not hurt, in N Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Soldiers fired on, not hurt, in N Ireland.

text.p: Two British soldiers were fired at but not hurt in an attack against their vehicle in Antrim, Northern Ireland, police said on Friday.
This weekend marks the first anniversary of the end to an Irish Republican Army ceasefire -- and both tension and violence have been building in the province.
"We are investigating reports of a shooting incident outside Antrim this morning," a police spokesman said.
He said an unmarked military vehicle was struck by three bullets on a road near Belfast's international airport.
"The two occupants -- both soldiers -- were unhurt and did not stop," the spokesman said. "When they did get out of the vehicle, they saw three strike marks on the side."

On Thursday night police said they had found a suspected IRA mortar near the town of Lurgan of the sort used by the guerrillas in their 27-year war to end British rule of the province and reunite it with the Irish republic.
